note: Structured case summaries for the DISCLOSURE case files. Claims are recorded as claims; status labels are defined at /cases/.

statusLabels.explained: An official finding or a well-documented cause accounts for the main evidence. Loose ends may remain.
statusLabels.disputed: An ordinary explanation is on the table with real support, and credible people still reject it, or the record is too thin to settle it.
statusLabels.unexplained: No explanation fits the record yet. The label says nobody has shown what it was, and nothing more.

cases.name: US Navy UAP videos (FLIR1, Gimbal, GoFast)
cases.title: The Gimbal, GoFast and FLIR UFO videos explained
cases.dateDisplay: FLIR1: 14 November 2004. Gimbal and GoFast: January 2015. The Navy gave 21 January 2015 for both, in a statement carried by The Black Vault.
cases.place: Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego (FLIR1); off the US East Coast (Gimbal, GoFast)
cases.coordsNote: Approximate. FLIR1 only: about 100 miles southwest of San Diego per CBS News. Gimbal and GoFast were off the US East Coast; AARO gives the eastern coast of Florida for GoFast.
cases.witnesses: Navy aircrews. Public figures: Cmdr. David Fravor and Lt. Cmdr. Alex Dietrich (the 2004 sighting), Chad Underwood (the pilot who filmed FLIR1) and Ryan Graves (who served in the Gimbal squadron).
cases.duration: Short infrared clips. Longer recordings and the radar data have not been released.
cases.evidence: Infrared targeting camera video with on-screen flight data and cockpit audio, plus aircrew testimony, some of it given under oath.
cases.officialFinding: Department of Defense, 27 April 2020: the phenomena remain characterized as unidentified.’ (war.gov) AARO, 6 February 2025, on GoFast: the object did not move at anomalous speeds. (aaro.mil) FLIR1 and Gimbal are listed as unresolved.
cases.statusReason: AARO resolved GoFast as ordinary in 2025. FLIR1 and Gimbal are still listed as unresolved, and the aircrews reject the leading explanations.
cases.verdict: The three Navy videos are genuine military footage, and the Pentagon officially released them in April 2020. None of them is proof of an alien craft. In 2025 AARO found that GoFast showed an ordinary object at about 13,000 feet. FLIR1 and Gimbal are still listed as unresolved, and analysts argue both show distant jets.

explanations.name: GoFast: an ordinary object made fast by parallax
Gimbal: glare from a distant jet, turned by the camera mount
FLIR1: a distant aircraft flying away
Something the military still cannot identify

cases.name: Al Taqaddum object ("Jellyfish UFO")
cases.title: The Jellyfish UFO video explained
cases.dateDisplay: 23 October 2017, per AARO. Early press reports in 2024 gave 2018.
cases.coordsNote: Approximate: Al Taqaddum Air Base, west of Baghdad.
cases.witnesses: Base personnel watching a sensor feed. One former Marine controller at the base has spoken publicly about what he saw.
cases.duration: The full video AARO released runs 17 minutes 27 seconds.
cases.evidence: Thermal infrared video from a sensor on a force-protection aerostat, a tethered surveillance balloon, operating at 2,700 feet.
cases.officialFinding: AARO case resolution, 8 September 2025: AARO assesses with high confidence that the Al Taqaddum object did not exhibit anomalous behavior or capabilities. (aaro.mil)
cases.statusReason: AARO matched the object to a balloon cluster moving with the wind and released the full video. The water claim has no support in it.
cases.verdict: The Jellyfish video was filmed over Al Taqaddum Air Base in Iraq in October 2017 and leaked in January 2024. In September 2025 the Pentagon’s UAP office, AARO, concluded with high confidence that it shows a cluster of balloons drifting with the wind. The claim that it went into the water is not shown in the full video.

explanations.name: A cluster of balloons
A transmedium craft

cases.name: New Jersey drone sightings
cases.title: What were the New Jersey drones?
cases.dateDisplay: First reports 18 November 2024, per the FAA and FBI. Picatinny Arsenal police logged reports from 13 November. Reports peaked in December 2024.
cases.place: New Jersey, United States, mainly Morris and Somerset counties
cases.coordsNote: Approximate centre of Morris County, where the FAA says the first reports came from.
cases.witnesses: Residents, police and trained security staff at two military bases. The FBI received more than 5,000 tips.
cases.duration: About six weeks of reports, from mid November to late December 2024.
cases.evidence: Tips, phone video and visual reports. Federal agencies said electronic detection did not back up the visual sightings.
cases.officialFinding: DHS, FBI, FAA and DoD, December 2024: We have not identified anything anomalous. (faa.gov) White House, 28 January 2025: the drones were authorized to be flown by the FAA for research and various other reasons. (rollcall.com transcript)
cases.statusReason: Federal agencies matched the reports to drones, aircraft and stars. The operators of drones confirmed over two bases were never publicly named.
cases.verdict: Federal agencies traced the New Jersey drone reports of late 2024 to lawful drones, manned aircraft and even stars, and found nothing anomalous. In January 2025 the White House said the drones had been authorized by the FAA for research. Drones confirmed over two military bases were never publicly traced to an operator.

explanations.name: Manned aircraft mistaken for drones
Lawful drones and stars
Drones authorized by the FAA for research
A wave of reporting

cases.name: Ariel School sighting
cases.title: The Ariel School UFO incident
cases.dateDisplay: 16 September 1994, during the mid-morning break, about 10:00 to 10:15 am.
cases.coordsNote: Approximate: the town of Ruwa, about 20 km from Harare.
cases.witnesses: About 60 children, 62 in most accounts, aged roughly 6 to 12. No adult saw it: the teachers were in a staff meeting.
cases.duration: Accounts vary. A 1995 summary by Mack’s research associate gives about 15 minutes.
cases.evidence: Children’s accounts recorded days to weeks later, drawings collected by the headmaster, filmed interviews. An instrument check of the site found nothing.
cases.officialFinding: None. No government, police or military investigation or finding was found. The only investigators were a UFO researcher, a journalist and a psychiatrist.
cases.statusReason: Many former pupils stand by their accounts. Skeptics argue suggestion shaped them, and no physical trace or adult witness exists.
cases.verdict: On 16 September 1994, about sixty children at Ariel School in Ruwa, Zimbabwe, reported a craft and a small figure beyond their playing field. No adult saw it and no physical trace was found. Many of those children, now adults, still stand by what they reported. Skeptics point to suggestion, group dynamics and a fireball seen two nights earlier.

explanations.name: Something physical that the children saw
Suggestion and group dynamics
A country primed by a fireball
A prank

cases.name: Travis Walton abduction claim
cases.title: The Travis Walton abduction story
cases.dateDisplay: 5 November 1975, about 6:15 pm. Walton phoned family from Heber just after midnight on 11 November. One local paper gives 10 November.
cases.place: Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest near Heber, Arizona
cases.coordsNote: Approximate: the town of Heber, Arizona. The Turkey Springs work site was in the forest nearby.
cases.witnesses: A seven-man Forest Service thinning crew: Walton, foreman Mike Rogers and five others. Walton and Rogers are public figures.
cases.duration: The crew described a sighting of moments. Walton was missing for about five days.
cases.evidence: Crew testimony, Walton’s own account and a series of polygraph tests with conflicting results. No physical evidence.
cases.officialFinding: None found. The Navajo County Sheriff’s Office investigated, but no closing report or finding was located, and there was no federal inquiry.
cases.statusReason: Walton and his crew stood by the account for decades. A skeptic argued it was a hoax to escape a work contract, and the lie-detector results conflict.
cases.verdict: Travis Walton says a craft took him from an Arizona forest on 5 November 1975 and that he woke aboard it. He was missing for about five days. Six co-workers say they saw a beam strike him. No physical evidence was ever produced, and the polygraph record cuts both ways. No official body issued a finding.

explanations.name: An abduction, as Walton describes it
A hoax to escape a work contract
A real light, then something in the mind

cases.name: Shag Harbour UFO incident
cases.title: The Shag Harbour UFO incident
cases.dateDisplay: 4 October 1967, at night. Reports put the first calls to the RCMP around 11:00 pm and the object on the water around 11:20 pm.
cases.coordsNote: Approximate: the village of Shag Harbour. The object was reported entering the water a short distance offshore.
cases.witnesses: An RCMP corporal and six other witnesses, per the National Defence memo. Later accounts count about a dozen people at the shore, plus fishermen. RCMP Const. Ron O’Brien has spoken publicly.
cases.duration: Minutes in the air. A light stayed on the water before it disappeared. The sea search ran through the night, and the navy dive search lasted about three days.
cases.evidence: Police and National Defence records, witness statements, and a trail of yellowish foam that searchers reported on the water. No debris was recovered.
cases.officialFinding: National Defence memo: divers failed to locate any tangible evidence. (Library and Archives Canada) The archives’ exhibition adds that National Defence identified this sighting as unsolved.
cases.statusReason: National Defence classed it as unsolved. Rescue officials ruled out a missing aircraft and flares, and the dive search found no debris.
cases.verdict: On the night of 4 October 1967, witnesses including an RCMP corporal saw a lit object come down into the sea off Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia. No aircraft was missing, and navy divers found nothing. National Defence classed the sighting as unsolved. It is one of the few UFO cases with Canadian government records behind it.

explanations.name: A plane crash
A meteor or marine flares
A submarine or a secret aircraft
An unknown craft that moved underwater
